body:
<!-- /sc:issue feature template (simple). Filled from the description and a standard /sc:analyze pass. -->

## Feature Summary

Thank you, Ryan, for the issue watcher and the standing coordinator ([PR #707](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/707), merged on master). They are the design, and this issue keeps them as they are. This follows owner ruling R38, which keeps the merged design, in `.dev/releases/backlog/issue-watcher-zero-setup/requirements.md` (the owner's watcher decisions). Nothing is replaced.

Could `/sc:issue` set up everything an issue needs for the watcher except the approval? This question comes from gaps 1 and 7 of [issue #761](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/761), the list of 18 possible watcher and coordinator gaps.

## Problem Statement

To get one issue worked by the watcher, a person today has to remember and do six separate things by hand:

1. Assign the issue.
2. Set the Project Status to Research, Spec, Plan or Debug.
3. Set the Pipeline field.
4. Add the trigger label.
5. Give the per-issue grant: the owner's yes in chat, which the agent then records. `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` (the rules for workers and coordinator actions) explains this grant.
6. Set the `Approved` field.

Today nothing in `src/` (the shipped source) writes the Pipeline field, moves an issue from Backlog to Research, applies the trigger label to an issue, or sets the `Approved` field. A source search for Project writes found one Project-field writer: `superclaude issue-pipeline complete`. Its file, `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/complete.py` (the coordinator's completion writer), moves Status to In review after success. It does not prepare an issue for work.

`/sc:issue --create` sets the issue type and the Complexity issue field. Its command file, `src/superclaude/commands/issue.md` (the issue command's options and limits), says it will not write any other issue field. `/sc:issue --claim` assigns the issue to the running login. But the watcher only finds issues that are already assigned, so assignment is still a hand step before the watcher can claim it.

Creating the trigger label on the repository is different from applying it to an issue. `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/repo_init.py` (first-run repository setup) already creates the repository label when it is missing. That does not complete hand step 4.

Clay works through agents, not by clicking in GitHub, and expects 20 or more pull requests a day. At that volume the routine has to be one command, or the setup steps will be skipped or done wrongly.

## User Story

As an owner who works through agents, I want one command to prepare an issue for the watcher on my say-so, so that I do not have to remember each setup step and approval stays a separate human step.

## Proposed Solution

### Proposal, as a question

Could `/sc:issue --create` and `/sc:issue --claim` set the Status, Pipeline field, assignment and trigger label on the owner's say-so, and stop before `Approved`? The approval would stay a separate human step. Whether an agent could help with that step belongs to the sibling issue about the two approvals, not this one.

For the owner and Ryan: which of the five items (assignment, Status, Pipeline, trigger label and per-issue grant) may an agent set, and under which GitHub login?

Answer these related issues first:

- [Issue #722](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/722): the owner and AI helpers share one GitHub login, so GitHub and our checks cannot tell who approved.
- [Issue #698](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/698): the approver rule accepts an approval comment from an assignee or an id in the approvers file, and the launch guard only reads command text.

### Moving pieces (gap 7)

The chain today is the watcher, the claim tab, the coordinator, the worker, two stores, two approvals, grant rows, the ship gate, and the Status and labels. Can that chain be made shorter for the person who has to remember it?

Could we run a small simplification review after the related questions above are answered? Its answer depends on them. Our search of issues, pull requests and plan files found no review of the whole chain, but that absence is UNVERIFIED. The check that settles it is a cross-check of all repository issues, pull requests and plan files for a review covering this whole chain, not just one route.

[Issue #733](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/733), removing human plan approval for unattended `/sc:implement`, simplifies one route only. [Issue #716](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/716), missing coordinator features, keeps the existing claim and store path as the baseline. This review would respect that baseline and the merged design.

### Open questions

1. May the agent that sets these items use the same login as the owner ([issue #722](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/722), shared-login approval identity)? If not, which account?
2. Which GitHub Project id and which field ids does the command read, and where are they configured?
3. UNVERIFIED: whether a login with less than admin rights can write the Project fields and the label. The check that settles it is one trial write on a test issue under that login.

## Acceptance Criteria

These are proposed conditions if the owner and Ryan answer yes, not approval to build now.

- [ ] Record the owner's and Ryan's answers on which of the five setup items an agent may set and under which login. Resolve the shared-login and approver-rule questions first.
- [ ] Define where the Project and field ids come from before implementing any Project write.
- [ ] One `/sc:issue --create` or `/sc:issue --claim` invocation performs the permitted setup on the owner's say-so. This includes the agreed Backlog-to-Research move when that is the requested starting Status.
- [ ] The command stops before setting `Approved`. The approval remains a separate human step. Any per-issue grant is recorded only from the owner's actual yes, under the agreed rules.
- [ ] Complete the small review of the whole chain after the related answers. Record whether any person-facing steps can be shortened without replacing the watcher, coordinator, claim or store path.

## Out of Scope

- The approval itself, including setting the `Approved` field.
- The watcher code.
- Changing who may approve.
- Replacing the merged design.

## Components Affected (from `/sc:analyze`)

The standard codebase pass found the missing setup path in the issue command and skill. The watcher reads the required inputs but does not prepare them. Its read-only boundary must remain intact.

- `src/superclaude/commands/issue.md`: issue command options and field-write limits. Its current limits would need to match any agreed setup behaviour.
- `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/SKILL.md`: create and claim rules, including who may make outward writes. Create currently does not assign the issue.
- `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/refs/create.md`: create steps and allowed GitHub writes.
- `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/refs/claim.md`: claim steps, including assignment to the running login.
- `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/refs/labels.md`: current mode-label, issue-type and Complexity rules. Claim currently changes no label or field.
- `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/scripts/`: existing helper folder for origin checks, ClickUp assignment and Orca handoff. It has no Project setup helper today. If agreed, this is a place to add the setup work without changing watcher code.
- `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/complete.py`: reference for validated Project reads and Status writes. Keep its completion-only role.
- `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/github.py`: read-only watcher discovery and Project reads. Discovery requires both the trigger label and assignment. Reference only, not a change target.
- `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/defaults.py`: central defaults, including a repository-to-Project map and the trigger label. Reference for the configuration question, not a change target.
- `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/cycle.py`: validates the per-repository `project_id`. Reference for the configuration question, not a change target.
- `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/repo_init.py`: creates the repository's trigger label and checks that the approval field exists. It does not apply the label to an issue or approve it. Reference only.
- `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`: per-issue grant and coordinator-only outward-action rules. Any setup plan must obey them.

The pass used Glob, Grep and Read. This was a static pass, not a live permissions test or a test-suite run.

## Related Issues/PRs

- [Issue #761](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/761): list of 18 possible gaps; this question covers gaps 1 and 7.
- [Issue #722](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/722): shared GitHub login and approval identity; answer first.
- [Issue #721](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/721): claim estimate refactor in the same skill.
- [Issue #698](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/698): approver rule and command-text-only launch guard; answer first.
- [Issue #716](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/716): missing coordinator features; preserves the existing claim and store baseline.
- [Issue #733](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/733): removes human plan approval on the unattended implementation route only.
- [PR #707](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/707): merged watcher and coordinator work on master; kept, not replaced.

The duplicate search found no open issue that covers this request.

## Priority

High: set by Clay; the trigger is "other work is blocked": the routine of working 20 or more pull requests a day through the watcher is blocked without one command.

## Fix approach

Repo: IronbellyOrg/IronClaude. Base branch: master.

Commands, in order, only after a yes to the proposal: `/sc:workflow "Implement the agreed issue setup answers" --depth standard --handoff none`, then `/sc:implement <the plan path returned by workflow>`, then `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3 --base master` with the resulting branch and PR details.

Assumption: if the proposal is accepted, setup should be safe to repeat and should report each failed or missing write instead of claiming full success.

Steps, in order:

- Step 1: get the owner's and Ryan's answers to the questions above (issue 722 and issue 698 first). These are the shared-login and approver-rule decisions. Record the allowed setup items, account, Project configuration and grant handling before changing the issue command or skill.
- Step 2: if the answer is yes, run `/sc:workflow` to plan those agreed writes in `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/` (the issue skill package). Use its existing `scripts/` helper folder for validated setup operations. Compare the Project selection checks in `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/complete.py` (the completion writer), without changing its completion role. Keep `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/` (the watcher package) unchanged.
- Step 3: if yes, run `/sc:implement` on that plan. Update `src/superclaude/commands/issue.md` (options and limits), the skill's `SKILL.md` (shared rules), and its `refs/create.md`, `refs/claim.md` and `refs/labels.md` (create, claim and classification steps) together. Add only the agreed assignment, Status, Pipeline, trigger-label and grant handling. Do not infer an approval from a setup request or write `Approved`.
- Step 4: test repeated setup and partial failures. Read back the agreed fields and assignment before reporting success. Keep outward writes with the authorised session, not a drafting worker. Run the checks below and sync the development copies with `make sync-dev`.
- Step 5: after the related answers, carry out the small simplification review. Respect issue 716's existing claim and store baseline and issue 733's limited unattended-route change. Record the result, including a decision to keep the chain unchanged if that is the answer.
- Step 6: run `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3` with master as the base after the checks pass and the owner has authorised submission. Do not merge as part of this work.

## Test plan

Assumption: automated tests use fake GitHub replies. A live write is a separate, explicitly authorised test on a test issue under the chosen login.

- Tests to add or change: extend `tests/commands/test_issue_command.py` (command options and limits) and `tests/skills/test_issue_protocol.py` (skill steps and boundaries). Cover both create and claim setup, the chosen login, and the explicit stop before `Approved`. Add fake-runner tests for any agreed setup helper in the existing `tests/skills/` folder (skill helper tests).
- Setup cases: check the agreed Backlog-to-Research move, each permitted Pipeline value, assignment and trigger-label application. Check a repeated invocation, missing or ambiguous Project items, missing fields or options, denied writes and partial success. Confirm read-back failure is not reported as success. Check that a grant comes only from the owner's recorded yes, not from the command merely running.
- Approval boundary: on a fresh unapproved test issue, successful setup must leave `Approved` unset and must not bypass either approval. Existing approvals must not be rewritten by setup. Keep `tests/issue_watch/test_security_invariants.py` (watcher write boundaries) and `tests/issue_pipeline/test_complete.py` (completion comments and Status moves) passing without changing watcher behaviour.
- Regression gate: run `uv run pytest`, `make lint`, `make sync-dev` and `make verify-sync`. These check the full suite, lint, development-copy refresh and copy consistency. No tests were run during this drafting pass.
- How a reviewer verifies: read the answers before reviewing the code. In the authorised test, use the chosen login and agreed command on a test issue. Read back assignment, Status, Pipeline and trigger label. Verify `Approved` was not set and no grant or approval was invented. Repeat the command and check the failure cases with fake replies. For the less-than-admin-rights question, one authorised trial write on that test issue settles whether that login can write the Project fields and label. Do not treat this issue body as permission to perform that write.

title: [FEATURE] Let `/sc:issue` set up everything an issue needs for the watcher except the approval
